key_insight: GlotOCR Bench shows that modern OCR systems still generalize poorly beyond a small set of high- and mid-resource Unicode scripts by providing a standardized evaluation across 100+ scripts using real multilingual text renderings.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of comprehensive, multilingual OCR evaluation — current benchmarks focus on a few scripts, hiding failures on many low-resource and diverse-script languages.
method: Assemble a benchmark covering 100+ Unicode scripts drawn from real multilingual texts.
Render images using Google Fonts with HarfBuzz shaping and rasterization, producing both clean and degraded variants to simulate real-world conditions.
Evaluate existing OCR models across scripts and image degradations to quantify generalization gaps and reveal script-specific failure modes.
impact: Provides a reproducible, wide-coverage evaluation that helps practitioners identify where OCR models fail, prioritize resources for underrepresented scripts, and drive development of more inclusive OCR systems.
visual_elements: World map or grid highlighting covered scripts (heatmap of script coverage / number of samples per script).
Bar chart or violin plot comparing OCR accuracy per script, with clean vs degraded variants side-by-side.
Rendering pipeline diagram: text corpus → font selection (Google Fonts) → HarfBuzz shaping → rasterization → OCR model.
Before/after sample tiles: clean vs degraded images with predicted vs ground-truth text overlays to illustrate typical errors.
paper_title: GlotOCR Bench: OCR Models Still Struggle Beyond a Handful of Unicode Scripts
paper_authors: Amir Hossein Kargaran, Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Jana Diesner, François Yvon, Hinrich Schütze
